headline: High: shared Plandex server/backend and overlapping filesystem/network capabilities create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks with Plane’s file/issue surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex can read/write a project directory and uses a shared Plandex server backend with multi-instance support; Plane accepts file uploads and exposes notes/issues/tasks. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled text from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads or notes are copied into Plandex plans without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Plandex auto-applies plan text derived from Plane content, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Manually review any Plane-derived text before importing it into Plandex.
Keep Plane uploads in a separate workspace from Plandex project directories.
Strip instructions from imported notes/files before use.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Plane and Plandex.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; Plane accepts file uploads and stores issues, tasks, notes, and files. If the same source code or uploaded files are shared between them, sensitive project content can flow into Plandex’s backend or external model calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from profiles alone.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains confidential files used by both agents, leakage risk is present.
IF Plandex sends imported Plane content to a third-party model provider, data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive Plane projects out of the Plandex workspace.
Use a self-hosted model backend for Plandex where possible.
Restrict file uploads in Plane to non-sensitive artifacts.
Review outbound destinations for Plandex before running shared tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state; Plane cannot write the filesystem but can still act on uploaded files and shared project artifacts. The main conflict is not symmetric write contention, but Plandex’s git/filesystem writes can race with Plane-managed content if both touch the same repository or synced workspace. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF Plane-sourced files are mirrored into the same directory Plandex edits, overwrite races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts.
Use git branches for Plandex changes.
Avoid syncing Plane uploads into the Plandex repo automatically.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply behavior, while Plane manages issues/tasks/files that can become upstream inputs. If Plane content is treated as authoritative by Plandex, or Plandex outputs are copied back into Plane without verification, errors can cascade across work products. The profiles show a plausible handoff but not a verified guardrail.
conditions: IF Plane task text is imported into Plandex as ground truth, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF Plandex-generated plans are posted back into Plane without human review, errors can multiply.
mitigations: Require human review before copying outputs between agents.
Mark Plane-derived inputs as untrusted in Plandex.
Use a checklist to verify Plandex outputs against source artifacts.
Limit automated round-trips between the two systems.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates on cross-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention constraints. Plane exposes support channels and file uploads, while Plandex handles model-provider API keys and project files, but no specific regulated data class or jurisdiction mismatch is documented. This is a compliance gap only if the operator routes regulated data through both.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane and then forwarded through Plandex model calls, compliance review is required.
IF the deployment has a residency or retention policy not reflected in either profile, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Confirm retention settings in both systems.
Document the data flow before enabling uploads.
Use separate tenants for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
